raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix compilation caching for the Transformers backend by running Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing PyTorch graph caches.

Decorated HF `forward` methods can fail model-AOT serialization. Disabling model AOT alone is insufficient: direct artifact lookup can reuse stale compiled code when decorator state changes between processes.

Following the review suggestion, HF opts out through `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`. The option is passed explicitly through `init_backend` to the backend, compiler manager, and adaptors:

- Skip model AOT, mega artifacts, and direct artifact loading/saving, including existing cache-index lookup.
- Retain PyTorch graph caching and initialize persistent Inductor/Triton cache directories.
- Preserve native AOT caching, including native EAGLE3 drafts under an HF target.

This replaces the earlier `CompileCachePolicy`, owner ContextVar, and loader changes. The opt-out applies in `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`; cache-disable settings remain respected. HF does not attempt forced model-AOT loading when opted out.

Related to #50128, specifically compilation caching. Follows the graph-caching recommendation in #53295 and preserves the cache-relocation behavior from #52142. This addresses HF cache routing rather than the cache-key API migration in #39517 or empty-artifact validation in #56879.

## Test Plan

- Fresh-process regression for changed decorator closure state, warm graph-cache hits, and repeated forward calls, covering both Inductor adaptors.
- Native AOT save/load after an opt-out module runs under the same configuration.
- Functorch configuration restoration on normal/exceptional exit and hash calculation; bypass of existing direct-cache metadata and handles.
- Three HF models and a native control under two cache-persistence protocols; real TP=2 and full HF-target/native-EAGLE3 generation.
- Full Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K evaluation under the batch-invariant compilation configuration described below.

## Test Results

### Warm startup: 8.9%–10.5% less time with persistent caches

Before is main at `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`; After is the smaller implementation described above.

Single L20, TP=1, BF16. Each model/backend/version/protocol has **1 cold + 5 fresh-process warm runs**, alternating A/B order. Values are `LLM(...)` initialization **median [min, max] in seconds**, excluding imports.

For the primary protocol, both versions receive persistent Inductor/Triton cache-directory settings. Caches are isolated by model/backend/version, and each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. Worker paths are verified because vLLM may redirect Inductor to its own persistent subdirectory.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 20.344 [20.105, 20.953] | **18.204 [17.595, 18.343]** | **10.52%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 15.570 [15.160, 16.111] | **14.121 [13.734, 14.297]** | **9.31%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 27.830 [27.769, 28.155] | **25.355 [25.183, 25.572]** | **8.89%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.857 [11.723, 11.978] | 11.719 [11.659, 12.030] | Ranges overlap |

The HF results are consistent in magnitude with the earlier 8–10% observation. No native speedup, throughput improvement, or TTFT improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Supplement: only VLLM_CACHE_ROOT persists</summary>

Inductor/Triton directory overrides are unset; each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. This measures the case where only the vLLM cache root persists, rather than ordinary same-user restarts.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 30.274 [30.041, 31.056] | **18.180 [17.794, 18.358]** | **39.95%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 25.188 [24.725, 25.983] | **14.109 [13.875, 14.304]** | **43.98%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 37.718 [37.262, 38.034] | **24.810 [24.631, 25.560]** | **34.22%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.909 [11.545, 12.693] | 11.958 [11.618, 12.532] | Ranges overlap |

The **34.2%–44.0%** reduction is specific to this protocol. Compared with explicit lower-level caches, HF Before is 9.62–9.93 s slower; After differs by 0.011–0.545 s. Worker paths and cache counters support a cache-persistence explanation, without establishing per-kernel attribution. Independently compiled caches and shared-host load also limit cross-protocol attribution.

Native median changes are −1.17% with explicit caches and +0.41% with root-only persistence. Ranges overlap in both protocols; no consistent native regression or speedup is established.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cold timings and reproducibility</summary>

| Model / backend | Explicit Before / After, s | Root-only Before / After, s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 46.855 / 44.519 | 47.267 / 45.283 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 37.518 / 35.636 | 37.459 / 36.782 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 56.375 / 54.423 | 56.104 / 52.939 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 51.503 / 51.999 | 52.575 / 51.835 |

- **96/96 starts completed; all 96 cache checks passed.** No samples were discarded. These are new measurements of the smaller implementation, not reused smoke timings.
- Baseline: `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`.
- Measured patch SHA256: `5edec6ae4c933e25df921c1c1d045b2ff277c0d8c56ed473ac12f99a2b2bf4eb`.
- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Transformers 5.15.1, Triton 3.7.1. A/B use identical hashes for the five rebuilt dense-runtime extensions.
- BF16, FlashAttention, seed=0, max model length=512, max batched tokens=512, max sequences=8, memory utilization=0.8, CUDA graph sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, four CPU/compilation threads.
- Raw AOT/mega/standalone flags are enabled; cache-disable and force-load are disabled. No batch invariance or additional deterministic controls are enabled. All workers use `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.
- Fixed physical L20 GPU 4, checked idle before every start. Runs were serial within the task; the host was not CPU-exclusive. A/B never share compiled artifacts; remote graph caches are disabled.
- Cold means an empty compilation cache. OS page caches were not cleared; model-file verification may warm them. Single cold observations and five warm samples do not establish statistical significance.
- Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. TinyLlama and Qwen3-14B snapshots are identified by per-file SHA256.

</details>

### Correctness and cache behavior

- **HF:** all After warm performance runs hit FX/AOTAutograd caches; model-AOT/direct-artifact save/load counts remain zero.
- **Native:** all cold runs save AOT; all five warm runs per version/protocol load it with zero model-AOT recompilations. Separate forced-load checks also pass.
- **TP=2:** Qwen3-0.6B HF completes cold/warm initialization and generation on both versions. Both After ranks record three FX and three AOTAutograd hits on warm start, with separate rank cache directories.
- **EAGLE3:** full generation with Qwen3-0.6B HF and `Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3` completes across cold/warm processes. The HF target uses graph caching; the native draft saves AOT on cold start and loads it on warm start.
- **Cache disable:** separate HF cold/warm checks retain compilation while recording zero FX/AOTAutograd cache hits and zero model-AOT/direct-artifact saves or loads.

Performance runs generate the same 32 prompts after initialization, using batch sizes 1/4/8, greedy decoding, and up to 64 tokens. **All 128 comparisons pass the existing repository helper without relaxed tolerances; 124/128 contain token-sequence differences.** Each comparison covers 32 prompts; this count is not a prompt failure rate or an accuracy measurement.

| Model / backend | Explicit: comparisons with token differences | Root-only: comparisons with token differences | Helper failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 16/16 | 16/16 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 14/16 | 16/16 | 0 |

Each group includes ten within-version cold/warm comparisons and six corresponding A/B comparisons. The helper checks first-divergence tokens against the other output's top-5; it does not establish full-sequence or accuracy equivalence.

### Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K

All **1,319 questions**, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 256-token generation limit. Before cold, After cold, and After warm each score **519/1319 (39.35%)**, with **identical per-question answers and complete token sequences**. Each run has 3 invalid answers and generates 132,670 tokens. After warm records **29 FX graph hits and 29 AOTAutograd hits**.

This uses batch invariance with compilation enabled, max model length=4096, max batched tokens=2048, and max sequences=8. Batch invariance disables model AOT upstream; mega/standalone remain enabled. This evaluation does not establish quality equivalence under the default AOT-enabled configuration or for Qwen3-14B. Evaluation timings are excluded from the performance results.

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and coverage limits</summary>

Default runs contain token differences across versions and between cold/warm starts within a version, despite passing the repository helper. Separate smaller-implementation smoke comparisons also pass the helper, with these token-sequence differences among 32 prompts:

| Path | Before cold → Before warm | Before cold → After cold | After cold → After warm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HF | 4/32 | 6/32 | 3/32 |
| Native | 4/32 | 1/32 | 4/32 |
| HF TP=2 | 7/32 | 5/32 | 6/32 |
| EAGLE3 | 2/32 | 2/32 | 3/32 |

These smoke comparisons are separate from the 128 performance-run comparisons above. Cache-disabled HF runs also differ on 5/32 prompts, showing that cache hits are not necessary for output variation; this does not rule out all effects of the patch.

The largest common-prefix logprob difference in the performance matrix is **4.312496** for Qwen3-14B: an unselected token has logprobs −13.250004 and −17.5625, while both runs select the same token at that position. This is not evidence of an incorrect selected token, but the differences should not all be described as negligible rounding. Operator-level attribution has not been established.

The batch-invariant GSM8K result is separate evidence with its own configuration limits. Full Qwen3-14B quality evaluation has not been repeated for this implementation. Earlier implementation-specific numerical controls and quality results are not counted as current validation.

Testing covers the recorded dependency environment and L20 GPUs. Required dense-runtime components were rebuilt from pinned source, but this is not a full wheel/Rust build, every optional extension, or full upstream CI. ROCm execution and a separate real `model_impl=auto` → HF resolution check remain unverified. The independent TinyLlama breakable-CUDA-graph issue is outside this patch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and results</summary>

Relevant suites ran with fresh vLLM cache roots and the verified task environment:

```bash
.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/compile/test_config.py

.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_decorator.py \
  tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py
```

- **127 passed, 1 skipped:** configuration tests 89 passed; decorator/AOT/compiler-interface tests 38 passed, 1 skipped.
- Six targeted mutations were detected: index read, direct load, configuration restoration, second forward, disabled native AOT, and hash-configuration restoration.
- A subsequent test-only isolation fix mocks adaptor cache initialization in the old-index test. A focused rerun including an environment-state probe reports **5 passed**; both index-read/direct-load mutations remain detected. Product code was unchanged. These counts are not additive, and the full suite was not rerun after this test-only change.
- Twelve applicable Python hooks passed on the smaller implementation; ruff, formatting, mypy, and diff checks were rerun after the isolation fix. Full pre-commit was blocked by offline actionlint dependency installation; full CI is not claimed.
- Existing binary/unpacked artifact-relocation tests are retained. The ROCm adaptor call site was updated, but ROCm tests were not executed locally.

Performance harness: `performance_controller.py`, `run_models.py`, `model_probe.py`, `export_results.py`, and `final_audit.py`. Per-run commands, environments, source hashes, worker paths/counters, full outputs, and exit codes were retained alongside the 96-sample CSV.

</details>

Assisted by Astra.

Hi @zou3519 @hmellor, This PR implements the suggested graph-caching approach https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53295#pullrequestreview-5026765752: the Transformers backend runs Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing cached AOTAutograd/Inductor artifacts. Native model AOT caching is preserved.

Would you both mind taking a look? Thanks!

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @Taimys.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

@hmellor Thanks for the suggestion! Updated to use the decorator flag and removed the policy, ContextVar, and loader changes. The implementation is now limited to the compilation path and the HF decorator call. Validation results are updated in the description. Could you take another look?

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for picking this up and for the thorough validation. Graph caching instead of AOT for the Transformers backend is the right direction, but I think the implementation can be much smaller.

The Transformers backend already applies `support_torch_compile` itself (`transformers/base.py`), so the owner of the compiled module is known at decoration time. Instead of `CompileCachePolicy` + the ContextVar + the loader changes, could we add a decorator option (e.g. `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`), store it on the class, and pass it through `init_backend` to `VllmBackend`/`CompilerManager`? That handles the native EAGLE draft case for free and removes the `resolve()`/identity-check logic.

Smaller points:
- Make the flag a required argument in the compiler adaptors rather than defaulting to `resolve()`, so a missed call site can't silently fall back to the env policy.
- `bundled_autograd_cache=False` is patched in three places; passing the flag into `set_functorch_config()`/`_get_vllm_functorch_config()` would cover it once.
- Tests: please trim to behaviour, e.g. one warm-cache regression (changed decorator state recompiles instead of hitting a stale artifact) and one check that native AOT still saves/loads. Also pin `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE` in them; several fail on platforms where it isn't the default.
- Please rebase (conflicts with #52142 among others) and note AI assistance in the description per AGENTS.md.

@zou3519 does the decorator flag sound right to you?

Performance harness: `performance_controller.py`, `run_models.py`, `model_probe.py`, `export_results.py`, and `final_audit.py`. Per-run commands, environments, source hashes, worker paths/counters, full outputs, and exit codes were retained alongside the 96-sample CSV.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for picking this up and for the thorough validation. Graph caching instead of AOT for the Transformers backend is the right direction, but I think the implementation can be much smaller.

The Transformers backend already applies `support_torch_compile` itself (`transformers/base.py`), so the owner of the compiled module is known at decoration time. Instead of `CompileCachePolicy` + the ContextVar + the loader changes, could we add a decorator option (e.g. `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`), store it on the class, and pass it through `init_backend` to `VllmBackend`/`CompilerManager`? That handles the native EAGLE draft case for free and removes the `resolve()`/identity-check logic.

Smaller points:
- Make the flag a required argument in the compiler adaptors rather than defaulting to `resolve()`, so a missed call site can't silently fall back to the env policy.
- `bundled_autograd_cache=False` is patched in three places; passing the flag into `set_functorch_config()`/`_get_vllm_functorch_config()` would cover it once.
- Tests: please trim to behaviour, e.g. one warm-cache regression (changed decorator state recompiles instead of hitting a stale artifact) and one check that native AOT still saves/loads. Also pin `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE` in them; several fail on platforms where it isn't the default.
- Please rebase (conflicts with #52142 among others) and note AI assistance in the description per AGENTS.md.

@zou3519 does the decorator flag sound right to you?
